title: Economy-aware prefill demultiplexer with micro-fallback lanes
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem:
We need a scheduling policy that reduces per-token cost and tail latency variance for mixed workloads without compromising fairness across tenants. Current prefill/decode arbitration uses static lanes (latency-first vs throughput-first) and a kernel selection step that doesn't incorporate request-level economics or a fast fallback mechanism for short interactive queries.

Proposal summary:
Design and implement an "economy-aware demultiplexer" that routes requests at prefill time into dynamically chosen micro-lanes based on an economy score: a weighted function of expected tokens remaining, per-kernel cost curve, latency SLO risk, and tenant priority. Each micro-lane will be paired with a micro-fallback fastpath: a conservative kernel + attention-optimization configuration that favors low tail latency for short/interactive requests. Longer or cost-sensitive batchy requests will be steered to high-throughput kernels and aggregated batching windows.

Key ideas and innovations (distinct from existing schedulers):
- Economy score per-request: expected_tokens_estimate * kernel_cost_estimate + latency_penalty(term) where latency_penalty is derived from SLA slack and queue depth.
- Micro-fallback lanes: a small number (2-4) of persistent fastpaths using conservative kernel and attention-optimization settings (smaller KV cache footprint, proactive KV prefetching, attention-sparsity hints) that prioritize 99th percentile latency.
- Kernel selection integration: the demultiplexer queries a lightweight kernel-latency model to predict per-kernel latency and cost for the request's sequence-length distribution and attention density probe. The kernel hint travels with the request into the arbiter so execution can be steered without additional probing.
- Attention-sparsity probe: for long-form or probabilistic workloads we add a short prefill probe (first 8 tokens) to estimate softmax sparsity and branching factor to improve kernel selection accuracy. The probe is optional and budgeted into economy score.
- Fairness budget: per-tenant rolling budget that ensures economy routing cannot starve low-usage tenants; a credit-based boost is applied to tenants under-served over the last hour.

Acceptance criteria:
- Perf: median latency for interactive queries (<40 tokens) reduced by at least 8% on internal benchmark A, 99th percentile reduced by 10% on same benchmark, while overall per-token GPU time does not increase by more than 5% for mixed workloads.
- Cost: simulated unit token cost across mixed workloads shows >=10% reduction for PLG traffic patterns (short-chat dominant) compared to baseline.
- Fairness: no tenant experiences >15% increase in latency compared to baseline when running at 5th percentile of historical usage (verify with fairness test harness).
- Safety: rolling rollout with canary for 5% of traffic, automatic fallback to baseline lane on anomaly.

Implementation plan:
1) Simulation harness (2 sprints): extend microbatch simulator to incorporate economy score, kernel-cost models, and attention-sparsity probe. Run synthetic workloads and customer-derived traces.
2) Kernel latency model (1 sprint): small regression model per-device-type that returns latency and cost estimate for sequence-length and attention-sparsity buckets.
3) Demultiplexer service (1 sprint): lightweight routing layer integrated into prefill stage that annotates requests with lane and kernel_hint.
4) Micro-fallback fastpath implementations (1 sprint): runtime profiles for conservative kernel settings + attention prefetch; telemetry hooks.
5) Canary rollout + monitoring (1 sprint): dashboards, alerts, automated rollback.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Extra probe overhead for attention-sparsity may increase cost for some requests. We'll gate probe to cases where uncertainty is high (long tail of sequence-length/role-change patterns).
- Kernel-latency model is approximate; mispredictions could route critical requests to slower lanes. Mitigation: conservative bias to choose low-latency lane when uncertainty high, and fast detection+fallback.
- Fairness complexity: per-tenant budgets increase state; keep budget window coarse (1h) and use periodic compaction to limit memory impact.

Telemetry and experiments:
- Experiment groups: control (baseline), demux-only (routing without probe), demux+probe, demux+probe+fairness.
- Key metrics: median/99p latency per query-length bucket, GPU token-seconds, kernel hotness heatmap, tenant starvation events, rollback triggers.

Deliverables:
- Design doc (Confluence link), simulator config and results, runtime changes (PRs), canary playbook, dashboards for runtime-1.21 release.
